acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ford Foundation archive was deposited at the RAC in 2011. Ford Foundation records, correspondence, reports, program files, and officers' papers were transferred to and accessioned by the RAC beginning in 2011. Accessions continue as necessary.
This material was transferred to the RAC in one accession in 2023 and was ingested by the RAC as Accession 2023:055.
This material was given to the Ford Foundation by Nick Menzies with a 2020 certificate of gift.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This collection holds a set of files Nick Menzies created when he worked as the Program Officer for Rural Poverty and Resources in the Ford Foundation's Beijing, China Office between 1990 and 1995. Menzies gifted these materials to the Ford Foundation in 2020.

The collection consists of one series of subject files that primarily consist of field notebooks from Menzies' work in the Yunnan province in China and calendars recording his appointments. A few of these materials date earlier to 1988 when Menzies worked in Yunnan for Winrock International. Winrock was funded by the Ford Foundation for those activities. Menzies also included a USB drive in his gift to the Foundation that contains files from his time in the Beijing Office as well as an article from 2016 regarding his work in Yunnan.

Menzies was the second Program Officer to serve in his position at the Ford Foundation's Beijing Office, and through his previous work with Winrock International, he had worked in China since the Office opened in 1988. This collection therefore helps document the development of the Foundation's Rural Poverty and Resources Program in China from its inception. The materials show how social forestry management was a large focus of this work.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Ford Foundation established its field office in Beijing, China in 1988. Prior to opening that office, the Foundation managed to directly engage the country for several years through collaborating with the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS) to make grants. This work began in 1979 after China and the United States established diplomatic relations. CASS then helped the Foundation to negotiate the establishment of an office in China and was made the Foundation's host when the office was approved. Within the Foundation, the Beijing Office was situated within its larger Asia Programs.

Throughout its history, the Ford Foundation's Beijing Office has engaged in a number of different program areas including economics, legal reform, China-U.S. relations and other international relations work, public policy, environment and development, the impact of China's global development, poverty reduction, the social impact of urbanization, education, women, reproductive health, and civil society.

did.unittitle: Subject files
did.physdesc: The bindings on some of the field notebooks have started to deteriorate. Notebooks should be handled carefully.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains subject files Nick Menzies created and maintained when he worked as Program Officer for Rural Poverty and Resources in the Ford Foundation's Beijing, China Office between 1990 and 1995. There are also earlier materials from when Menzies worked for Winrock International in China between 1988 and 1989 and some later digital media material Menzies added to the collection when he gifted the records to the Ford Foundation in 2020. Through these different records, the series documents the development of the Foundation's Rural Poverty and Resources Program in China from the time the Beijing Office opened in 1988 to when Menzies left China in 1995. The materials especially highlight the Foundation support for social forestry management in the Yunnan province.

There are three main parts of the series. The first part includes the collection gift of certificate, contents description, and digital media. The certificate contextualizes Menzies' work in the Beijing Office and explains how the materials were transferred to the Foundation. Researchers can use the certificate and the file-level contents description on the collections inventory to gain a stronger understanding of the other materials in the series. There is a description of the file directory of the digital media item. The files on this item include maps, program reviews, field visit reports, presentations, and grant related documents. Additionally, it contains a 2016 article.

The next part of the series comprises a set of field notebooks Menzies used when he worked in China between 1988 and 1995. The notebooks span across both his positions at Winrock International and the Ford Foundation. They document program field visits throughout various counties in Yunnan and other locations in China. Some of these visits were to grantees and potential grantees. A few other items are interspersed throughout the notebooks. They include maps, loose notes, correspondence, and business cards.
The last part of the series contains a group of appointment calendars Menzies used while working in China.
